summary: The revised candidate addresses all 21 mandatory design criteria with a concrete versioned native-fork and per-actor runtime mechanism. No mandatory contradiction, omitted criterion, invented required protocol field or unauthorized implementation scope expansion was found. This pass does not establish runtime feasibility or any native/publication/confinement pass.
role_read_confirmation: All three sources reopened completely and exact digests returned to manager after round-2 activation. Original role pair and inherited settings preserved.

criteria.criterion: Neutral starter has no live identity/branch set, standing grant, schedule or autonomous-write permission.
criteria.assessment: Neutral identity, selection, branch, entitlement, schedule and autonomous-write defaults are preserved.
criteria.required_verification: policy/classification source and existing reported F-POLICY

criteria.criterion: Missing, malformed, expired or incompatible selections produce precise unavailable/blocked diagnostics.
criteria.assessment: Strict read-only diagnostics remain; storage/authentication, epoch and unsupported-bound failures are explicitly named.

criteria.criterion: Project specialization is capability-only; standing entitlements remain absent until deliberately accepted at adoption.
criteria.assessment: Capability-only specialization and prior protected acceptance remain distinct from operational authority.

criteria.criterion: AGENTS.md, README sections, generated wiki and Task responses have distinct owners and update routes.
criteria.assessment: The exact AGENTS, README section, generated wiki and Task-history routes remain with their existing owners.

criteria.criterion: Overrides, generators, stable identities and protected sections resolve conservatively; unknown/mixed targets hold unsafe edits.
criteria.assessment: Stable identity, source/section bindings, protected classification floor and ambiguous-target holds are retained; actual profile proof remains pending.

criteria.criterion: Grants bind actor/project/branch/policy/source/payload/scope/owner and freshness; valid standing entitlements avoid redundant approval.
criteria.assessment: Exact grants and accepted standing entitlements are preserved; new calls bind the current connection/load epoch without changing old grant meaning.

criteria.criterion: Candidate-controlled code and environment cannot alter broker policy, credentials or effective approval logic.
criteria.assessment: Protected runtime cwd/config/imports, per-actor companions and enforced tool profiles keep approving code outside candidate control by design; native enforcement remains a required gate.

criteria.criterion: Broker routes canonical mutations to their existing helper owners and rejects arbitrary shell instructions.
criteria.assessment: Existing canonical helpers remain the publishers. New runtime controls are finite and event-specific; no raw shell, configuration or protocol proxy is introduced.

criteria.criterion: Caller identity comes from the trusted native request envelope and current manager binding, not an actor string in model arguments; workers cannot read private grants or broker credentials.
criteria.assessment: Protocol v2 separates broker run, connection, kernel process identity, thread/session and load epoch; actual transport creates live authority. Serialized observations and caller arguments cannot authenticate.

criteria.criterion: One controller/charter is selected per execution; reading a charter does not activate it.
criteria.assessment: One selected charter/controller and Director default remain explicit; reading a charter neither activates it nor transfers an owner.

criteria.criterion: Specialist responsibilities, qualifications, role reads, scope and stopping rules are explicit; generic Director use and category rules are preserved.
criteria.assessment: The qualified source role pairs, fresh catalog/fit checks, exact role reads, skill/tool checks and complete category rules are preserved.

criteria.criterion: New provenance is schema-versioned and validated; historical records retain bytes/meaning and unknown fields are rejected.
criteria.assessment: Explicit Task/protocol/observation/live-call version tuples retain legacy validation and history. Actual forkedFromId is not relabeled as AgentControl parentage or a collaboration receipt.

criteria.criterion: Curator bootstrap reserves exactly one manager, activates only the real receipt identity and relinquishes canonical Task writing.
criteria.assessment: A current canonical reservation precedes the actual fork request. Authentic creation correlation, metadata and child acknowledgement precede manager activation and sole-writer transfer.

criteria.criterion: Existing record/configuration schemas keep their meaning; any changed grant envelope has explicit version dispatch.
criteria.assessment: Existing owner record/config and grant envelopes retain meaning; their new nested protocol version is dispatched explicitly and unsupported combinations fail.

criteria.criterion: Only the current confirmed manager with exact operation scope can publish Curator knowledge; ordinary workers and forged provenance fail.
criteria.assessment: Only the current loaded manager/channel/epoch with exact Task generation, writer, role reads, source/payload/config and independent owner grant can publish. Older epochs and ordinary workers remain rejected.

criteria.criterion: Activation, manager/child discovery, supervision, interrupt and resume observations are mapped without forging collaboration receipts.
criteria.assessment: Event-specific delivery, conflict, observation, interruption, release and resume replace the current generic status-receipt conversion. Resume preserves the native ID and uses actual thread/resume.

criteria.criterion: Effective model/effort and independent contexts are checked; missing capabilities hold work.
criteria.assessment: Parent model/effort are explicitly propagated before fork creation, then compared with actual responses and loaded metadata. Identical completed history cuts and full input bytes are separately checked. Missing capability holds work.

criteria.criterion: Real observations establish identities, reservation-before-launch, one canonical writer, full required teams, settings inheritance and isolated solver input.
criteria.assessment: Stage 1 is clearly a narrow mechanism diagnostic. Full generic/complex/extra-complex teams, manager acceptance, dedicated implementation, isolated inputs and actual publications remain mandatory in the complete NP proof.

criteria.criterion: Capacity queuing preserves every required agent; uncertain or absent observations are named non-passes.
criteria.assessment: Local admission counts creating/loaded/unloading/uncertain runtimes; verified targeted runtime/helper closure may release only that local slot. Native IDs and queued roles persist, and uncertainty remains occupied.

criteria.criterion: Candidate writes to trusted policy/broker, canonical ledgers, control records, grants and credentials are denied by the enforced boundary.
criteria.assessment: Candidate read/write denial includes trusted runtime/helper/config/private/canonical storage and all exposed native channels. Paired positive/negative actual enforcement and final canary checks remain mandatory.

criteria.criterion: Malicious branch/diff/note/config, process execution and broker-request cases cannot gain authority or bypass publication.
criteria.assessment: The original malicious content, policy, grant, process, path, import and network cases remain, with added intrinsic control and helper-state probes tied to actual execution arguments/results.

mechanism_assessments.assessment: The pinned ThreadForkParams supports threadId, the mutually exclusive cut fields, model, config, cwd, permissions and runtimeWorkspaceRoots. It does not expose a direct effort or allowProviderModelFallback field; the candidate uses the supported config override for effort and explicitly does not invent the absent fields. The tagged fork constructor records forked_from_thread_id separately from parent_thread_id. The candidate preserves that distinction in a new dialect. Tagged source is supporting evidence only.

Thread/read loaded model and reasoningEffort fields describe configured settings, not per-turn telemetry. The design binds these precreation observations, compares fork response and loaded metadata, denies mismatch rather than repairing it, and still requires actual unavailable-model/fallback proof. StartThreadOptions defaults allow_provider_model_fallback to false and the tagged fork uses that constructor; this is not a pinned-binary proof. The required gate remains unproven.

The candidate correctly identifies persisted source history as a prerequisite and selects test-owned protected storage without guessing a relocation key. It requires non-model verification of the exact storage and existing supported account reuse, forbids credential copying/symlinking/reconstruction, user-task creation, new provider/login and silent normal-store fallback, and supplies named failures before charged work. The supplied packet establishes no successful storage/account combination. The route is a coherent conditional design, not a feasibility claim.

Both initial solvers use the same completed source cut and complete actual history/input digest. The candidate requires complete supported history reads without deleting model-visible differences, and separate actor-owned companions with real fixed-program store/load probes, cross-actor denial and reset-on-resume tests. Intrinsic peer/control routes remain disabled and tested through all exposed channels. No model self-report or artifact echo is accepted as execution proof.

mechanism_assessments.topic: Per-actor release, native unsubscribe and provider completion
mechanism_assessments.assessment: The candidate explicitly distinguishes interrupt/turn outcome, unsubscribe, native loaded state, verified runtime/helper process termination, owner reconciliation, broker authority closure and local admission release. Tagged unsubscribe only removes a subscription. Verified actor-owned process absence can free the selected local runtime slot while preserving the native identity; it does not prove remote provider completion or billing cancellation. Uncertain descendants or process identity prohibit release. A fresh runtime uses actual same-ID resume with a new load epoch, without a new fork disguised as resume.

The design addresses actual current incompatibilities: scalar receipt_sequence currently becomes a status notification, receipt() cannot represent an outbound fork response, native session binding assumes one connection, and unsolicited started identities enter the control map. Its explicit protocol-v2, per-connection/load-epoch pool and event-specific frame decoding cover creation, inputs, conflicts, reconciliation, resume and independent publisher guards, with old branches preserved.

The new proof packet must be independently materialized and assessed by the host. Stage 1 states twelve broker turn/start requests, twenty minutes, three loaded/creating runtimes and fixed I/O/stop limits as local selected bounds, not provider calls/tokens or host collaboration capacity. Production model_calls semantics remain unchanged and unsupported hard bounds block the relevant mode. The narrow diagnostic does not include real project publication and cannot replace full NP-001 through NP-014, independent memory/ontology grants or final-source repetition.

required_unproven_gates: Exact test-owned persistence/state isolation with the normal selected account and no credential copying or ordinary user task creation.
Actual pinned-binary fork, precreation model/effort/profile equality, unavailable-model no-fallback behavior, supported history cuts and restored dynamic callbacks.
Actual actor-private helper state and complete native tool/filesystem/process/network isolation with positive/negative observations.
Verified targeted runtime/helper termination, other-actor continuity, preserved native IDs and same-ID resume with stale-epoch rejection.
Full required category teams, authenticated manager handoff and independent owner publications, all adversarial cases and current final release source bindings.
